title: Scene Conflict Pressure
principle: A scene needs a present-tense pressure source: the character wants something now, and something resists that want.
use_when: Use when a scene feels descriptive, flat, or like setup without dramatic pressure.
checklist: Name what the character wants in this scene.
Name what blocks or complicates that want.
Make the obstacle visible through action, dialogue, or consequence.
End the scene with a changed situation, not only more information.
bad_patterns: The scene only explains background.
The character observes but does not choose or risk anything.
Conflict is abstract instead of present in the moment.
revision_strategy: Add a concrete obstacle or competing desire before adding more description.

title: Character Motivation Line
principle: Character behavior should follow a readable desire, fear, belief, or pressure established by the project materials and recent memory.
use_when: Use when a character acts conveniently, changes emotion too quickly, or makes a choice that feels author-driven.
checklist: Identify the character's immediate motive.
Check the motive against known character facts.
Show the motive through action or hesitation.
Make any change of mind respond to a new pressure or realization.
bad_patterns: A character changes position because the plot needs it.
The action contradicts established fear, loyalty, or goal without pressure.
Internal logic is explained after the fact instead of dramatized.
revision_strategy: Insert the missing pressure, memory, or cost that makes the choice feel necessary.

title: Dialogue Naturalness / 对白自然度
principle: Dialogue should sound like people pursuing goals under social pressure, not like exposition delivered in turns.
use_when: Use when dialogue feels stiff, over-explanatory, or interchangeable between characters.
checklist: Give each speaker a purpose in the exchange.
Let subtext carry part of the meaning.
Break exposition with interruption, avoidance, or misdirection.
Keep character voice consistent with status, mood, and relationship.
bad_patterns: Characters explain facts both already know.
Every line answers the previous line too neatly.
All speakers use the same sentence rhythm.
revision_strategy: Replace direct explanation with goal-driven lines, partial answers, and reaction beats.

title: Pacing Beat Change
principle: Each beat should change information, pressure, emotion, or position; repeated beats slow the chapter without deepening it.
use_when: Use when a chapter feels slow, repetitive, or padded after expansion.
checklist: Mark what changes in each paragraph or beat.
Cut or merge beats that repeat the same state.
Alternate observation with action or decision.
Let description earn its space by changing tension or understanding.
bad_patterns: Several paragraphs restate the same fear or atmosphere.
Description delays the next meaningful action.
A scene expands in word count but not in pressure.
revision_strategy: Compress repeated emotional notes and add a beat that changes the situation.

title: Scene Transition Continuity
principle: Adjacent scenes should preserve time, place, emotional state, and character intent unless the text deliberately signals a jump.
use_when: Use when scene-based generation creates a stitched or jumpy chapter.
checklist: Check where the previous scene ends and where the next begins.
Track time, place, character positions, and emotional residue.
Add a bridge sentence when the reader needs orientation.
Avoid repeating the same opening information in the next scene.
bad_patterns: The next scene starts as if the previous scene did not happen.
Time or location changes without a signal.
The same setup is repeated at multiple scene openings.
revision_strategy: Add one orienting bridge sentence or revise the next opening to inherit the previous scene's state.

title: Style Sentence Texture
principle: A chapter should maintain the project's chosen texture through sentence rhythm, sensory focus, narrative distance, and image density.
use_when: Use when prose feels generic, mechanically polished, or detached from the project's stated style.
checklist: Compare sentence rhythm against the project's style notes.
Check whether sensory details match the intended atmosphere.
Flag paragraphs where narrative distance suddenly shifts.
Prefer concrete image and action over abstract evaluation.
bad_patterns: The prose uses the same neutral rhythm in every scene.
Descriptions sound polished but not specific to the world.
Emotional statements replace observable behavior or image.
revision_strategy: Mark the places where rhythm, image choice, or narrative distance drifts from the style guide before suggesting localized changes.

title: Revision Focused Pass
principle: A useful revision pass identifies the highest-impact local fixes without rewriting the chapter or changing its plot function.
use_when: Use when a review needs to turn broad quality concerns into concrete next edits.
checklist: Separate structural issues from line-level issues.
Name the smallest edit that would improve each issue.
Preserve established plot events and character choices.
Prioritize fixes that improve clarity, pressure, or continuity.
bad_patterns: Feedback asks for a full rewrite when a local bridge or beat would solve the issue.
Suggested fixes introduce new plot facts not present in the outline.
The review lists vague preferences without an actionable edit.
revision_strategy: Convert each issue into a bounded edit instruction tied to a scene, paragraph, or transition.
